record.paper_title: Three open problems in function theoretic operator theory
record.original_question: Let p be a complex polynomial whose zeros all lie in the closed unit disk. For each zero a of p, must the closed disk {z : |z - a| <= 1} contain at least one critical point of p?

evidence.quote: The Sendov conjecture says that every disk of radius one centered at a zero
Despite important work, the conjecture remains open for polynomials of degree n

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $p(z)$ be a non-constant polynomial with complex coefficients all of whose zeros lie in the closed unit disk $\{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| \le 1\}$. Prove or disprove: for every zero $a$ of $p$, the closed disk $\{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z - a| \le 1\}$ contains at least one zero of the derivative $p'$ (i.e., at least one critical point of $p$).
artifact.status_search_result: The Sendov conjecture is known to hold for polynomials of degree at most 8 (Brown–Xiang and others) and, by Terence Tao (arXiv:2012.04125, Acta Mathematica 2022), for all polynomials of sufficiently high degree n ≥ n₀, where n₀ is an ineffective absolute constant. The conjecture remains open for intermediate degrees, so the full statement is unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Sendov's conjecture for sufficiently high degree polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Tao proves Sendov's conjecture for all sufficiently large degree n.
status_evidence.claim: Sendov's conjecture holds for all sufficiently large degree, proved by Tao.

status_evidence.title: Sendov's conjecture - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Proved for n < 9 and for sufficiently large n; remains open in general.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is verified for low and high degrees but remains open for medium degrees.
